analysis:
All supplied units are test code, a benchmark log parser, and a test-runner env export. No production source is in this batch, so the production VerifiedWeightHashStore, WeightHasher and GLM load changes behind these tests were not reviewed.

GLM5NextProviderLoopTests.swift (lines 194-219) covers the new load-time SHA-256 verification. It asserts that no WeightHasher pass runs, that the live hash equals the manifest aggregate, and that VerifiedWeightHashStore holds a record for the unchanged files. The test exercises behavior but does not change it.

VerifiedWeightHashStoreTests.swift checks that records are invalidated by a rewritten file, an appended or added file, and foreign or corrupt schema. It also checks that the record file is mode 0600 and that the per-model ID is respected. This is relevant to T-012, T-027 and T-013 (weight substitution). The tests suggest the identity check includes ctime or inode, which resists restoring mtime.

Unverified contract: the log line says the record is reused for a registration or advertised hash while "the load verifies again before serving". Whether the registration or advertised hash can be reported before the load verification completes, and whether a record could be forged by a same-user operator, is outside the evidence. A same-user operator who can edit records is already inside the T-012 operator trust assumption. Weight hashes are not hardware-attested, so no new boundary issue is evident. Integration should check that the record file written by production code uses 0600 and atomic writes, and that the DARKBLOOM_VERIFIED_WEIGHTS_FILE override cannot be set by an untrusted party in production. The scripts/run-provider-tests.sh export (line 22) only redirects test state to a temp dir, which is a safe change.

glm_load_timeline.py is an offline log parser. It reads local files, uses bounded regexes and an argparse path, and has no network or exec surface. Logs contain only truncated hash prefixes and model names, with no secrets. It is a low-risk addition.
